newsitem.title: FRANCE: French judge rejects cuts in Le Pen TV documentary.
newsitem.headline: French judge rejects cuts in Le Pen TV documentary.

text.p: A French judge rejected on Thursday a plea by far-right leader Jean Marie Le Pen that excerpts from his speeches be deleted from a television documentary about his National Front party to be broadcast later in the day.
Le Pen had argued that the film violated the law by improperly using public statements, insisting that his remarks were his private "literary property" which could not be used without his permission.
He also argued that the show invaded his privacy.

Judge Jean-Jacques Gomez said he had turned down Le Pen's plea on the grounds neither man had seen the documentary in question, entitled "Le Pen In Quotes" and to be broadcast on France 2 public television on Thursday evening.

The documentary producers say it analyses Le Pen's rise to political prominence and his ideology through extensive excerpts from his public statements made since 1984. Advance publicity has focussed on alleged inconsistencies in his statements about his personal history and wealth.
Taking excerpts from public statements "must conform with the rules governing the protection of literary property", the anti-immigration campaigner told the newspaper France-Soir.
"You could no more quote from a compilation of speeches made over the past 20 years...than you could use a novel under the pretext that its author had just written an article," he said.
Le Pen acknowledged he had not seen the documentary, but had gone to court on the basis of advance statements by the show's hosts.
He and supporters also complained that he had not been given air time to respond to the programme's findings.

In a press release, the National Front said that France 2, "a state channel and an organ of state propaganda, has resolved to proceed to the final solution: A trial of Le Pen without Le Pen, barred from the airwaves without being allowed to explain himself".

"As for the millions of French people who retain confidence in the National Front, they have only the right to continue to pay the TV license fee and see themselves insulted," the party statement said.
